behave-vsc.behaveWorkingDirectory.markdownDescription: The project-relative behave working directory (only required if it is not the project root).

behave-vsc.envVarOverrides.deprecationMessage: This setting is deprecated (renamed). Please use the "behave-vsc.env" setting.

behave-vsc.env.markdownDescription: Key-value pairs of environment variable overrides (or additions) to use when calling a behave command. This will apply to all behave tests within the project folder. Note that environment variables can also be set per run by using the `runProfiles` setting.

behave-vsc.args.markdownDescription: Additional arguments to pass to behave (or your customRunner). Note that the extension does not validate these arguments, so it is possible to break the extension and/or behave.

behave-vsc.featuresPath.deprecationMessage: IGNORED legacy setting. Feature paths are now discovered via the behave config file "paths" setting and the extension "behaveWorkingDirectory" setting.

behave-vsc.importedSteps.markdownDescription: Key-value pairs of additional imported steps to include for step navigation (e.g. step libraries that are not in your "steps" folder). Each pair has a key of a *project-relative* path to a folder inside the project, and a value of a regex (not glob) of step files to include.

behave-vsc.justMyCode.markdownDescription: If set to false (disabled), the debugger will step into external code when debugging a behave test.

behave-vsc.runMultiRootProjectsInParalle.markdownDescription: For multi-root workspaces only. If enabled, then when behave tests are started for more than one project, they are run at the same time. This setting should be in your `*.code-workspace` file.

behave-vsc.runParallel.markdownDescription: Specifies whether to create a separate behave instance for each feature and run those instances simultaneously (except when debugging). Leave this off for your initial run, then enable if you wish and your test setup supports it (i.e. your features are fully isolated).

behave-vsc.runProfiles.markdownDescription: A list of run profiles. These can be used to set tags, args and environment variables on demand for test runs. Also allows you to provide a customRunner script. See examples in documentation.

name.markdownDescription: The name of the run profile.

promptForTags.markdownDescription: If true, the extension will always prompt for adhoc tags to pass to behave. If false, the extension will just use the --tags included in `args` and/or `args.list`.

env.markdownDescription: Key-value pairs of environment variable overrides (or additions) to set when this run profile is executed.

inherit.markdownDescription: Whether or not to concatenate the `behave-vsc.env` setting. If false, the `envVars` setting will overwrite the `behave-vsc.env` setting.

vars.markdownDescription: Key-value pairs of environment variable overrides (or additions) to set when this run profile is executed.

args.markdownDescription: Additional arguments to pass to behave when this run profile is executed. These will overwrite any `behave-vsc.args` if `inherit` is false. Note that the extension does not validate these arguments, so it is possible to break the extension and/or behave.

inherit.markdownDescription: Whether or not to concatenate the `behave-vsc.args` setting. If false, the `list` setting will overwrite the `behave-vsc.args` setting.

list.markdownDescription: Additional arguments to pass to behave.

customRunner.markdownDescription: Custom Python script to invoke instead of the default behave command.

scriptFile.markdownDescription: The name of a custom python script file. Command becomes: `python <script> behave <your_args> <extension_behave_args>`. This file must be in the root of your behave working directory. Note that unless this is an actual behave runner (e.g. setup like behave-django's manage.py), you will not be able to debug tests except by custom means, e.g. attaching to the process via import debugpy and launch.json.

waitForJUnitFiles.markdownDescription: If true, the extension will wait for JUnit XML files to be created by the custom runner and update test results. If false, all selected tests will be marked as skipped.

behave-vsc.xRay.markdownDescription: If true, extension errors will show in popup windows, stack traces will be added to error logs in the Behave VSC output window, and diagnostics and performance traces will be added to console output. The console output is viewable via the vscode command `Developer: Toggle Developer Tools`. Diagnostic logs are noisy, and may have a small performance impact.

name: behave-vsc
description: Debug, Run and Navigate Python behave tests

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run compile-tests && npm run lint
